readme.markdown:
# Hyperping MCP Server

Official [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server for [Hyperping](https://hyperping.com). It exposes uptime monitoring, incident history, on-call schedules and reporting to AI agents over HTTP.

This is a **remote server**. There is nothing to install or self-host: point your client at the endpoint with an API key. This repository holds the registry manifest, the client configuration and the tool reference.

Full documentation: [hyperping.com/docs/mcp](https://hyperping.com/docs/mcp)

## Endpoint

| | |
|---|---|
| URL | `https://api.hyperping.io/v1/mcp` |
| Transport | Streamable HTTP, JSON-RPC 2.0 |
| Auth | Bearer token |
| Scope | One project per key |
| Tools | 26 (22 read, 4 write) |

## Quick start

1. In Hyperping, go to **Project Settings, API Keys** and create a `read_only` or `read_write` key.
2. Add the server to your MCP client (see below).
3. Restart the client, then ask it things like "what is down right now?" or "what was our uptime on the API monitor last month?"

### Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "hyperping": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://api.hyperping.io/v1/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer sk_..."
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### stdio clients

Clients that only speak stdio can bridge through [`mcp-remote`](https://github.com/geelen/mcp-remote):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "hyperping": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "mcp-remote",
        "https://api.hyperping.io/v1/mcp",
        "--header",
        "Authorization: Bearer sk_..."
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

## Tools

### Monitors

| Tool | Scope | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `list_monitors` | read | Paginated monitors, filterable by `up`, `down`, `paused`, `ssl_expiring`. |
| `get_monitor` | read | One monitor by UUID. |
| `search_monitors_by_name` | read | Case-insensitive substring search over names and URLs. |
| `create_monitor` | write | Create an HTTP, ICMP, port or DNS monitor. |
| `update_monitor` | write | Patch a monitor. Unspecified fields are preserved. |
| `pause_monitor` | write | Stop checks and alerts for a monitor. |
| `resume_monitor` | write | Resume a paused monitor. |

`delete_monitor` is deliberately not exposed. Use the dashboard or the REST API.

### Status and outages

| Tool | Scope | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `get_status_summary` | read | Up, down and paused counts, plus what is currently down and since when. |
| `list_outages` | read | Paginated outages, filterable by status, type or search term. |
| `get_outage` | read | One outage, with acknowledgements, description and root cause. |
| `get_outage_timeline` | read | Detection, cross-region verification, alert dispatch, acknowledgement, resolution. |
| `get_monitor_outages` | read | Outages scoped to a single monitor. |

### Reporting

| Tool | Scope | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `get_monitor_uptime` | read | Uptime percentage over a window, by hour, day, week or month. |
| `get_monitor_response_time` | read | Latency trend over a window. |
| `get_monitor_mttr` | read | Mean time to resolve, in seconds. |
| `get_monitor_mtta` | read | Mean time to acknowledge, in seconds. |

### Diagnostics

| Tool | Scope | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `get_monitor_anomalies` | read | Flapping, latency spikes and other detected anomalies. |
| `get_monitor_http_logs` | read | Recent HTTP probe logs, filterable by level. |
| `list_recent_alerts` | read | Up and down notifications over a date range. |

### On-call

| Tool | Scope | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `list_on_call_schedules` | read | All schedules, with rotation config and current on-call. |
| `get_on_call_schedule` | read | One schedule, with full rotation detail and linked policies. |
| `list_escalation_policies` | read | All escalation policies in the project. |
| `get_escalation_policy` | read | One policy, with step sequence, schedules and contact channels. |
| `list_team_members` | read | Project users, to resolve IDs coming from schedules and policies. |

To answer "who is on call for monitor X?", chain `get_monitor`, `get_escalation_policy`, `get_on_call_schedule`, `list_team_members`.

### Integrations

| Tool | Scope | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `list_integrations` | read | Slack, Telegram, Discord, PagerDuty, OpsGenie, Teams, webhook and others. |
| `get_integration` | read | One integration, with its channel-specific config. |

## Rate limits

Limits apply per project, and both windows are enforced.

| Method | Per minute | Per hour |
|---|---|---|
| `initialize` | 5 | 20 |
| `tools/list` | 30 | 200 |
| `tools/call` | 60 | 600 |

Open the session once and reuse it rather than calling `initialize` per request. Exceeding a limit returns a JSON-RPC error with a `retry_after_seconds` hint.

## Machine-readable spec

For a dense, agent-friendly spec covering tools, query patterns and response shapes, point your client at [`hyperping.com/mcp/llms.txt`](https://hyperping.com/mcp/llms.txt).

## Support

Open an issue here, or reach the team through [hyperping.com/contact/sales](https://hyperping.com/contact/sales).

toolsPreview.name: list_monitors
toolsPreview.description: Paginated monitors in the project. Optional status filter (up/down/paused/ssl_expiring).

toolsPreview.name: get_monitor
toolsPreview.description: Fetch a single monitor by its UUID.

toolsPreview.name: create_monitor
toolsPreview.description: Create a new monitor. Requires name+url; add "port" for port checks, "dns_*" for DNS checks.

toolsPreview.name: update_monitor
toolsPreview.description: Patch a monitor. Pass only fields you want to change; others are preserved.

toolsPreview.name: pause_monitor
toolsPreview.description: Pause a monitor — no checks run and no alerts fire. Same as update_monitor with paused=true.

toolsPreview.name: resume_monitor
toolsPreview.description: Resume a paused monitor. Same as update_monitor with paused=false.

toolsPreview.name: search_monitors_by_name
toolsPreview.description: Case-insensitive substring search across monitor names and URLs.

toolsPreview.name: get_status_summary
toolsPreview.description: Up/down/paused counts plus a list of currently down monitors with the timestamp they went down.

toolsPreview.name: list_outages
toolsPreview.description: Paginated list of outages in the project. Filter by status, type, or search term.

toolsPreview.name: get_outage
toolsPreview.description: Fetch a single outage by UUID, including acknowledgements, description, and root cause.

toolsPreview.name: get_outage_timeline
toolsPreview.description: Full activity timeline for an outage: detection, cross-region verification, alert dispatches, acknowledgement, resolution.

toolsPreview.name: get_monitor_outages
toolsPreview.description: Paginated list of outages scoped to one monitor. Convenience wrapper around list_outages.

toolsPreview.name: list_recent_alerts
toolsPreview.description: Alert notifications (up/down transitions) over a date range. Defaults to last 30 days.

toolsPreview.name: get_monitor_uptime
toolsPreview.description: Uptime percentage over a date window, aggregated and optionally per day/hour/week/month.

toolsPreview.name: get_monitor_response_time
toolsPreview.description: Response time latency trend over a date window.

toolsPreview.name: get_monitor_mttr
toolsPreview.description: Mean time to resolve (MTTR) per monitor over a date window, in seconds.

toolsPreview.name: get_monitor_mtta
toolsPreview.description: Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) per monitor over a date window, in seconds.

toolsPreview.name: get_monitor_anomalies
toolsPreview.description: Anomaly-detection output for a single monitor (flapping, latency spikes, etc.).

toolsPreview.name: get_monitor_http_logs
toolsPreview.description: Recent HTTP probe logs for a monitor, paginated. Useful to diagnose recent check failures.

toolsPreview.name: list_on_call_schedules
toolsPreview.description: All on-call schedules in the project. Each entry typically includes rotation config and current on-call.

toolsPreview.name: get_on_call_schedule
toolsPreview.description: One schedule by UUID with full rotation detail and the linked escalation policies.

toolsPreview.name: list_escalation_policies
toolsPreview.description: All escalation policies in the project. Use to find which monitors route alerts where.

toolsPreview.name: get_escalation_policy
toolsPreview.description: One policy by UUID. Reveals step sequence, linked schedules, and contact channels.

toolsPreview.name: list_team_members
toolsPreview.description: Users on the project, with names and emails. Use to resolve user IDs from schedules/policies.

toolsPreview.name: list_integrations
toolsPreview.description: All notification integrations in the project (Slack, Telegram, Discord, PagerDuty, OpsGenie, Teams, webhook, etc.).

toolsPreview.name: get_integration
toolsPreview.description: One integration by UUID, with its channel-specific config (channel name, webhook URL, routing, etc.).
